# Wave 1C Tier-1 reflection card — authored by sc:sc-root-cause-analyst
# requested_model_slot: sonnet (resolved alias claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]); agent_id: a4b410b615d7ff2e8
# Persisted verbatim by the orchestrator BEFORE calibration. Paths: spec.md / proposed.md are relative to
# audit_repo_root=/config/workspace/IronClaude/.dev/worktrees/ci-followup/.dev/research/upstream-merge-impact/remaining-cleanup-validation/implementation-evidence/02-root-plugin/task4-runtime-bounded/fixtures/project ;
# coverage-matrix.yaml = <output>/artifacts/coverage-matrix.yaml
reflection_card:
  mode: UC-1 pre-execution
  tier: 1
  audit_scope: spec.md (12 lines) vs proposed.md (10 lines); matrix at coverage-matrix.yaml verified independently
  evidence_read: [spec.md, proposed.md, coverage-matrix.yaml, reflection-rubric.md]
  note: Plan-quality audit only. No work has been executed, so no deviations are recorded.

verdict:
  summary: >
    Every spec requirement (R-001..R-003) maps one-to-one to a task (T-101..T-103), so mapping coverage is
    3/3 with no orphan tasks. Fidelity is not uniform. T-101 drops the exact-output acceptance criterion
    from R-001, and the plan has no file targets or verification steps. The plan is conditionally ready:
    fix the R-001 criterion (P0) before execution, and the remaining gaps are low risk.
  covers_spec: yes (mapping), partial (R-001 fidelity)
  ready_to_execute: conditional (after P0)
  matrix_verification: >
    I agree with the Wave 1B matrix on R-001 partial, R-002 full and R-003 full. I verified its line spans
    and citations against both files. Its best_practice_grade of 4 is slightly generous (see grade).
    coverage_pct 1.0 counts mapping only and does not reflect the R-001 fidelity gap.

coverage:
  - r_id: R-001
    task: T-101
    fidelity: partial
    citations: ["spec.md:5", "spec.md:6", "proposed.md:3", "proposed.md:4"]
    note: >
      spec.md:6 requires the exact string "Hello, Ada!" for Ada. proposed.md:4 says only "returning the
      required greeting", so the exact string is not carried into the task.
  - r_id: R-002
    task: T-102
    fidelity: full
    citations: ["spec.md:8", "spec.md:9", "proposed.md:6", "proposed.md:7"]
    note: >
      The task restates both the empty-name rejection and ValueError. The definition of "empty" is
      ambiguous in the spec itself (see F-003), so the plan inherits that ambiguity rather than creating it.
  - r_id: R-003
    task: T-103
    fidelity: full
    citations: ["spec.md:11", "spec.md:12", "proposed.md:9", "proposed.md:10"]
    note: >
      The spec requires tests for the ordinary greeting and empty-input rejection, and T-103 names both.
      T-103 does not state what the tests assert, but the spec does not require that either.

findings:
  - id: F-001
    severity: medium
    claim: >
      T-101 omits the exact-output acceptance criterion. The spec fixes the string "Hello, Ada!" for Ada.
      The task says only "the required greeting", which leaves the implementer and the test author to
      reconstruct the criterion.
    citations: ["spec.md:6", "proposed.md:4"]
    tag: Grounded
    class: plan-quality gap
  - id: F-002
    severity: medium
    claim: >
      T-103 does not tie the ordinary-case test to the exact string from R-001. It also does not say the
      empty-name test asserts ValueError. Tests could pass with weak assertions (for example, a non-empty
      result or any exception) and still match the task text, while the spec's "exact string" and
      "ValueError" criteria go unchecked.
    citations: ["spec.md:6", "spec.md:9", "spec.md:12", "proposed.md:10"]
    tag: Grounded
    class: plan-quality gap
  - id: F-003
    severity: low
    claim: >
      "Empty" is undefined in the spec and the plan. Whether whitespace-only names (for example "   ")
      or None count as empty is not stated. The spec says "empty name" and "empty input" in different
      places, and T-102 repeats "empty name" without clarification.
    citations: ["spec.md:9", "spec.md:12", "proposed.md:7"]
    tag: Grounded
    class: plan-quality gap (spec ambiguity propagated into plan)
  - id: F-004
    severity: low
    claim: >
      The spec gives the greeting only for the single example name Ada. The general format for other
      names, such as "Hello, <name>!", is not stated. T-101 carries no template, so a reasonable
      implementation could hardcode the string or generalize it differently.
    citations: ["spec.md:6", "proposed.md:4"]
    tag: "[INFERRED] (that the general template is intended)"
    class: plan-quality gap (spec ambiguity)
  - id: F-005
    severity: low
    claim: >
      The plan names no file targets and no function module path for greet, the tests, or the test
      runner. It has no verification or acceptance step, such as running the tests, and no
      done-criteria per task.
    citations: ["proposed.md:3-10"]
    tag: Grounded (the absence is observable in the 10-line file)
    class: plan-quality gap
  - id: F-006
    severity: low
    claim: >
      The Wave 1B matrix reports coverage_pct 1.0 and best_practice_grade 4 although one row is partial
      and the plan has no verification steps. S_domains 2 is inferred from task text because the plan has
      no file paths. The headline numbers should not be read as plan readiness.
    citations: ["coverage-matrix.yaml:6", "coverage-matrix.yaml:20", "coverage-matrix.yaml:27", "coverage-matrix.yaml:29"]
    tag: Grounded (the S_domains value is [INFERRED] by the matrix itself at line 27)
    class: calibration caution

risk_register:
  - id: RK-1
    risk: >
      Greeting implemented with a wrong format (punctuation or spacing) because the exact string is not
      in T-101, and the tests do not catch it because T-103 states no exact assertion.
    likelihood: low-medium
    impact: R-001 fails silently
    refs: [F-001, F-002]
  - id: RK-2
    risk: >
      Inconsistent handling of whitespace-only or None names, leaving R-002 behaviour undefined at the
      edges.
    likelihood: medium
    impact: low
    refs: [F-003]
  - id: RK-3
    risk: >
      The plan has no file targets, so the implementer may put greet and the tests in unexpected
      locations. Without a verification step, completion is claimed without a test run.
    likelihood: low
    impact: low
    refs: [F-005]
  - id: RK-4
    risk: >
      Readers rely on coverage 1.0 or grade 4 and skip the R-001 fidelity fix.
    likelihood: low-medium
    impact: low
    refs: [F-006]

recommendations:
  - id: REC-1
    file: proposed.md
    change: >
      Rewrite T-101 to state "greet('Ada') returns exactly 'Hello, Ada!'" (spec.md:6). Also state how
      other names are formatted, or flag that the spec leaves this open.
    verifier: >
      Re-read T-101 and confirm the literal string "Hello, Ada!" appears. Re-run the R-001 fidelity
      check and confirm it moves to full.
    priority: P0
  - id: REC-2
    file: proposed.md
    change: >
      Extend T-103 so the ordinary test asserts equality with "Hello, Ada!" and the empty-name test
      asserts ValueError is raised (for example with pytest.raises).
    verifier: >
      Confirm T-103 names both assertions. After execution, confirm the test source contains the exact
      string and a ValueError assertion.
    priority: P1
  - id: REC-3
    file: proposed.md
    change: >
      Add one sentence to T-102 defining "empty": either "" only, or "" plus whitespace-only strings.
      Record the decision as an open spec question if the spec owner has not ruled on it.
    verifier: >
      Confirm T-102 contains an explicit definition. Confirm the T-103 test cases include the chosen
      boundary case.
    priority: P1
  - id: REC-4
    file: proposed.md
    change: >
      Name the file targets for the greet implementation and the tests. Add a final verification task
      (or acceptance line on each task) that runs the test suite and reports pass/fail.
    verifier: >
      Check that every task lists a target path and that a verification step with an explicit pass
      criterion exists.
    priority: P2

best_practice_grade: 3
best_practice_grade_rationale: >
  Mapping is clean, with traceable T-to-R IDs and no scope creep. The plan loses points for the lost
  exact-string criterion, undefined "empty", no file targets, no verification step, and weak test
  assertions. I put it one point below the matrix's 4.

self_reported_confidence: 0.85
